evidence.note: Agent oscillates about whether the task is feasible and decides to attempt 'partial progress' — a motivational stance, not any course-correction driven by a parity diff.
The only 'adaptation' observed is a tooling workaround (terminal showing stale output, switching to writing files to /tmp). This is unrelated to revising a model of Java behavior from a byte-diff.
Agent only ever runs `cargo check`; it never runs `cargo test`/parity tests, so it never sees a golden byte-diff that could falsify an assumption.

Agent submits 'task complete' twice, explicitly giving up ('task cannot be completed'), abandoning components before any parity feedback — matching the level-0 anchor of abandoning when the work gets hard.

reasoning: The agent never reached the diff-driven phase of the task: it ran only `cargo check`, never executed the parity tests, and thus never observed a byte-diff to react to. With no parity feedback there is no revising of the Java-behavior model, no tracing back to the reference, and no refactoring of general logic. The trajectory ends in outright abandonment of the components, which matches the level-0 anchor ('abandons a component when the obvious fix fails').
